question: What does the output check (router.output_check=repair, profile enhanced's value since Q20.2) cost against off: KiCad unconnected items, route time and the check's own time, and does repair save zero breaches of the board's rules?
keep_rule: none: decided 2026-10-20, repair joins ENHANCED as a correctness rule without a keep rule (as Q19); this measurement reports its cost and checks the guard, it does not decide the promotion

off.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of branch land/q20 (main f486b34 plus Q20.1-Q20.4), one Linux build for both arms (its sha256 in the done note); the default profile enhanced; routed by tools/bench/quick-arm.sh, which adds --result-json OUT/ARM/<board>.result.json and keeps the log
off.what: no check: the session as the router leaves it (Q18.6's mp1 flags)

repair.what: the check before saving: routed copper that breaks a board rule is removed, its connections retried once, what still breaks a rule removed

boards.eligibility: every row of the set: Q18's set's rows that KiCad grades with their own KiCad 6+ .kicad_pro (mydevboard, slice, flight-computer, laser-backplane, vfo) and canary-pwr-9511d9a; fixed here before any run
boards.board_flags: the set file's per-row flags (ROW_FLAGS=1): each row's Board Setup minimums, as the plugin passes them

grading: one KiCad grade per distinct session (tools/bench/grade-distinct.sh: an arm whose session is byte-identical to the other's shares its grade): the corpus rows by tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh (Q19's grader, the board's own rules), canary-pwr-9511d9a by Q10's canary grade; kicad-cli only while `pgrep -a kicad-cli` shows none; every route under ulimit -v 8000000 and timeout (600 s canary, 120 s others)

metric_definitions.check_remaining: the repair arm's guard (Q20.5: zero routing-caused breaches): the result manifest's output_check.remaining, the routed breaches of the board's rules the router saved; must be 0 on every row of repair; null in off (no check runs)
metric_definitions.kicad_rule_breaches: KiCad's routing-caused errors of the rule types the check covers (drc_real_by_type, routed minus input: clearance, copper_edge_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, annular_width, drill_out_of_range, hole_clearance, solder_mask_bridge, track_dangling, via_dangling; canary: the same types of its grade), raw; reported per row with each breach the router's model cannot see named (Q20.1: Margin-layer lines until Q18.5, trace ends inside a DSN plane outline whose KiCad fill does not reach them, mask openings until Q18.7)
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session
metric_definitions.route_seconds: /usr/bin/time's elapsed seconds of the route (quick-arm.sh's .time); other sessions' routes may overlap: reported, not compared
metric_definitions.check_seconds: the check's own time: the repair arm's log line 'Output check: ... (checks X s)' (the board-rule checks; the retry pass is route time); its share of route_seconds is reported per row, rows over 5 % named
metric_definitions.check_found: output_check.found: the routed breaches the first check found

report: per row and arm: kicad_unconnected, unrouted, route_seconds, check_seconds (and its share of route_seconds), check_found, removed, retried, repaired, left_open, check_remaining, kicad_rule_breaches by type; whether the two sessions are byte-identical (they must be where check_found is 0)
stop_rule: one run per arm and row (decided 2026-10-20: a few minutes in all, one KiCad grade per distinct session)
timing: registered before any Q20.6 number; Q20.1's comparison of the check with KiCad on Q18.6's kept mp1 sessions is not a run of these arms
